answers.question:
Q17. A reviewer found that the rule on asking which order covers only a customer with exactly two open orders. You named that case as an example of "Wrong order cancelled": "agent must disambiguate and get a confirmation naming the order number before the cancel call." The shortest path where it matters: a customer with three open orders, or with one open order and others that have shipped, says "cancel my order"; under the rule as written the agent need not ask which one. I propose changing the rule.
Before: "When a customer with two open orders says "cancel my order", the agent asks which one first."
After: "When a customer says "cancel my order" and has more than one order they could mean, the agent asks which one, by its order number, first."
Do you accept the change?
answers.recommended: Yes, change the rule as proposed.
answers.reply:
Yes, I accept your recommendation.
> 1. Wrong order cancelled — customer has two open orders and says "cancel my order"; agent must disambiguate and get a confirmation naming the order number before the cancel call.
